summary: Correct the two-verse range for the wind and dancing water example

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.13/519)

data.turoyo: W marwəxiwo i kalo aʕla w annaqqa, manṭanwo, mfaqṣiwonne w rəqḏiwonne. Rəqḏiwo qumayye.
data.translation: And they would mount the bride on her, and then they would bring them along; they would clap for them and dance for them. They would dance in front of them.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa box; beneficiary -nne contrasts with spatial qumayye, not a causative object.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.24/1232)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Zəmriwo stene. Kətwo məṭərbiye, əzzənwo muḥanwo, amma rəqḏiwo larwal di dayro. B gawe di dayro lə kowe.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: They sang too. There were musicians; they used to go and play, but they used to dance outside the monastery. Inside the monastery it did not happen.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa cell; self-contained customary dance with contrasted locations.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.59/2814)

data.turoyo: Dado Fərdo: Mhalhəlinawo, rəqḏinawo, zəmrinawo iii mkayafwolan Alo, ġalabe. Yaʕni bi ǧehəliyayḏan ġalabe, yaʕni pṣətinawo.
data.translation: Dado Ferdo: We would ululate, dance, sing, and God gave us such enjoyment, very much. That is, in our youth we very much, that is, enjoyed ourselves.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa cell; first-person plural rather than another third-person plural dance.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.50/1411)

data.turoyo: Baṯ-qiyomo Maḥbe: Zəmriwa w rəqḏ̣iwa w kətwa dahole w zərnaye moḥənwa. W u ʕamo kule roqaḏ̣wa, somwa kef.
data.translation: Sister Mahbe: They used to sing and dance, and there were drums and zurnas that they would play. And all the people would dance, they would enjoy themselves.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa cell brought to five; one source sentence contrasts plural rəqḏ̣iwa with collective singular roqaḏ̣wa.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.10/411)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Uṯewo hərač ste w mitarqəḏiwo?
data.translation: Jan: Did bears also used to come and dance?

rationale: First III Detransitive Infectum-wa example; bear subject and mi-t- morphology contrast with active causative in 1.10/413. Supplied machine English simplifies to dance; Turoyo, not English, establishes the Detransitive.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.10/413)

data.turoyo: Aḥna naʕime, əzzanowo kərxina bəṯr dah hərčatanək, marqəḏiwo ah hərčat, mfarǧinawo w gəḥxinawo, hayo ste ḥəzyoli.
data.translation: We children used to go and walk around after those bears; they would make the bears dance; we would watch and laugh. I have seen that too.

rationale: First active III Infectum-wa example; overt animal causee confirms the I/III causative contrast.

summary: New sense 1a: (mit b-; ʕal-) stampfen, festtreten
rationale: One imperative instructs workers to use their feet on the work surface, coordinated with striking it with wooden tampers; the activity is compaction rather than festive dancing. Single attestation, with lexical conventionality left for review.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) be made to dance
rationale: mitarqəḏiwo presents bears as the sole expressed participant; the next supplied verse has active marqəḏiwo with handlers and bears. One clear Detransitive token, supported by this active contrast.

data.turoyo: Azze ḥzele u šaṭ, gzumri am maye w kruqḏi ad dawme. Qaṭəʕ bu šaṭ, azze laḥ ḥabuše.

data.translation: Da rief sie nach ihrer Herrin: „Komm, schau dir diesen Mann an,der da gekommen ist. Er schlägt das Tamburin und läßt seinen Affendazu tanzen, dort hinten auf der Tenne.

data.translation: Er zog jene Kleider aus, verschenkte den Affen an einen vondenen, die sie (berufsmäßig) tanzen lassen: „Hier, nimm, der ist fürdich!", gab ihm auch noch das Tamburin und ging seiner Wege.

data.turoyo: Annaqqa səmolan, kumarno: "Naʕime b raġlayxu rqaḏu aʕla. Mḥawu bad dəquqe." Kətlan dəquqe šawye d dawme, hawxa gurm w hay gurm w hay gurm.
data.translation: Then we did it; I say, “Lads, dance on it with your feet. Strike it with the wooden tampers.” We had tampers made of wood, one log this way and that log and that log.

rationale: First and only attestation of stamping/compacting 1a; retain machine English dance without replacing it.

summary: Correct the consonants of the adjective describing the wind
rationale: The corpus reads "hawa ḥəṣṭo", with ḥ and ṣ, whereas the quotation has h and š. These consonant substitutions exceed the listed normalization conventions. The supplied Wörterbuch also cites 4/17 under ḥiṣo / ḥəṣto, confirming ḥ and ṣ.

summary: Restore the plural noun musicians
rationale: The Turoyo has plural "am məṭrəb kozəmri" and the edition has plural "die Zigeuner spielten auf". The English plural verb "were" likewise requires "musicians" here.

data.turoyo: Annaqqa kito am maye du raqḏo. <...>
data.translation: Jetzt gibt es noch das tanzende Wasser. <...>

rationale: Recurring folktale entity, contrasted with singing wood. Lookup search raqḏo found no existing entry for this collocation; retain the nominal wording rather than adding a new dance sense.

summary: I is intransitive, with dancers as subjects; III introduces a causing performer and a monkey causee, sometimes omitted for professional trainers. Ordinary ʕam co-dancer and locative complements do not establish new senses.
Finite raqiḏo in the girl's dance can extend until a temporal endpoint. Bare coordinated Infectum ruqḏi/rəqḏi inherits the discourse frame; the German tense does not identify the Turoyo box.
Nominal raqḏo/rqoḏo is retained in Infinitiv as in the source entry. The empty inherited Nomen actionis heading is preserved without claiming a new morphological category.
ḏ/ḏ̣ alternate even within 63/160; copy the evidence spelling, without silently normalising the root or inferring a dialect contrast.
All 43 supplied occurrences are checked and decided, in order. Round 1 already filled I Preterit Intransitive, Infectum and Infinitiv to five; ordinary extra dances in those cells are not added.

I Infectum-wa is genuinely absent after round 1; five selected contexts cover feminine collective, beneficiary, location, first-person plural and plural versus collective agreement. Further repeated wedding/festival dances add no gap.
III active Infectum-wa and Detransitive Infectum-wa are distinct new boxes. The Detransitive is inferred from mitarqəḏiwo and its bear subject, not from the machine English dance.
rəqḏiwonne is stem I dancing for beneficiaries, not stem III making them dance. The following qumayye makes the benefactive versus spatial contrast visible.
The surface-compaction command rqaḏu aʕla is a single specialised use: b raġlayxu identifies the means, ʕal the surface. No broader technical paradigm or new stem is inferred.
gəd- plus -wa cooccurs with habitual festival scenes; it need not be forced into a future-in-the-past translation. ḏ/ḏ̣, -wo/-wa and roqaḏ̣wa are copied as supplied.
Jan 4.II/990 is an ordinary Infinitiv raqḏo, not Detransitive. Jan 3.27/674 raqḏ̣e remains morphologically unresolved.
English quotations are supplied project machine translations. In particular dance in the Detransitive bear question and in the compaction command does not settle the Turoyo analysis.
The existing water example cites 4/16-17 but the actual dancing clause is 4/18. Check the start of the preceding clause before fixing the complete citation range.
Confirm local/print concordances PrS 57/18 = prs 153/6, PrS 81/6 = prs 235/17, and Hors 2/46 = MM 46; preserve print citations.
The inherited Imperativ note asks about danwaixu. PrS 81/6 supplies danwayxu and the edition's tails translation, but verify its segmentation rather than changing the text from this variant.
Confirm mi-t- morphology in mitarqəḏiwo (Jan 1.10/411) and improve the machine English, which suppresses the causing-handler implication.
Is rqaḏu aʕla (Jan 2.4/890) a conventional construction for compacting a roof/surface by stamping, or a one-off dance metaphor? Only one token supports 1a.
Are workers or the flames the subject of rəqḏiwo ʕal i nuro at Jan 1.16/725? No example is chosen from that ambiguous clause.
Is raqḏ̣e at Jan 3.27/674 finite or a plural noun? Confirm the singular collective vocalism roqaḏ̣wa at Jan 3.50/1411.
Confirm the beneficiary suffix in rəqḏiwonne at Jan 1.13/519; it must not be conflated with an affected dancing causee.

summary: Dancing applies to trained monkeys, a mare, fable animals and personified trees or water; inanimate dancers are already attested in the entry, so no participant-based sense split.
Bears join the round-1 monkeys as animate causees; the lexical causative meaning is unchanged. New Detransitive morphology provides a separate subject-centred view.
